prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: Thực đơn quán phở (language vi).
Grid: 4 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes.
Measured content facts (text px at 13px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "Món" · longest unbreakable unit 31px · widest one-line content 94px
  col 2: header "Giá" · longest unbreakable unit 52px · widest one-line content 52px
  col 3: header "Thành phần" · longest unbreakable unit 42px · widest one-line content 1335px
  col 4: header "Ghi chú" · longest unbreakable unit 54px · widest one-line content 370px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 504px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 504px wide (column widths sum to at most 503px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 504px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Several designers worked independently on this table. You see their final layouts, anonymised as Layout P, Layout Q, Layout R, Layout S, Layout T, Layout U, in that order after the overview: Layout P, Layout Q, Layout R, Layout S, Layout T, Layout U.
Measured facts:
Layout P: column widths [115, 73, 210, 105] px · table 504×857 px · row heights [33, 154, 114, 134, 114, 134, 174] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 504 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout Q: column widths [95, 73, 225, 110] px · table 504×817 px · row heights [33, 154, 114, 134, 114, 114, 154] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 7 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 504 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout R: column widths [88, 73, 236, 106] px · table 504×777 px · row heights [33, 154, 94, 114, 114, 114, 154] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 7 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 504 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout S: column widths [105, 73, 225, 100] px · table 504×817 px · row heights [33, 154, 114, 134, 114, 114, 154] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 7 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 504 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout T: column widths [88, 73, 232, 110] px · table 504×777 px · row heights [33, 154, 94, 114, 114, 114, 154] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 7 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 504 px viewport (no scrolling)
Layout U: column widths [115, 73, 205, 110] px · table 504×857 px · row heights [33, 154, 114, 134, 114, 134, 174] · column headers on >1 line: 0/4 · tallest cell 8 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 504 px viewport (no scrolling)

Compare them side by side. For each layout name its strengths, its faults and the spatial logic behind it (how it distributes space and why). Do not just pick a winner: you may combine the strengths of several layouts, propose something new, or overturn all of them. Propose up to 3 new designs that you expect to be better than every layout shown; if you believe one shown layout cannot be improved, say so in "best" and propose fewer or none.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"analysis":[{"layout":"name","strengths":"","faults":"","spatial_logic":""}],"insights":"what the comparison teaches about this table","best":["names of the best layout(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"idea":"what it combines or changes, and why"}]}
